task_instance: Apply the parallel-feature-development skill to a concrete feature ('Saved Searches' on a React/TS + Node/Express + Postgres stack with 3 implementer agents): decompose it into parallel work streams with per-file ownership, an interface contract, conflict-avoidance rules, an unblocking stub, and a branch/integration strategy.
evidence: This is a planning/strategy skill whose deliverable is a text decomposition plan, which this text-only runtime fully supports. Created sample input feature-spec.md (the feature request a user would supply). Produced parallel-plan.md, the actual deliverable, applying every core element the SKILL.md specifies: (1) file-ownership strategy chosen (by-module) with a one-owner-per-file table for team-lead/implementer-1/implementer-2/implementer-3; (2) the Cardinal Rule 'one owner per file' enforced and the barrel/index-file conflict trap assigned to a single owner per the skill's troubleshooting rule; (3) a read-only interface-contract file (SavedSearch/CreateSavedSearch/SavedSearchService) that both sides import but neither modifies, with the broadcast-before-change rule to prevent signature drift; (4) integration pattern selected and justified (Hybrid = vertical slices + one horizontally-owned shared contract); (5) a staging stub implementing the contract so UI and tests do not block on the real API (the skill's finished-early remedy); (6) branch strategy chosen with reasoning (single feature branch, since 3 agents + non-overlapping module folders, matching the skill's small-team guidance). Verified by re-checking the produced plan against each SKILL.md section (File Ownership Strategies, Conflict Avoidance Rules, Interface Contracts, Integration Patterns, Branch Management, Troubleshooting) and confirming each prescribed element is instantiated concretely for the chosen feature. No code execution, binary output, network, or credentials were needed. Files: feature-spec.md, parallel-plan.md, result.json in the work directory.
